hints.content:
We are given that the first printer takes $\pink{30}$ seconds to warm up.

The table of values for the second printer shows that for each decrease of $\blue{16}$ in $\blue{\text{Pages}}$, $\pink{\text{Duration}}$ decreases by $\pink{20}$ seconds. The time it takes the second printer to warm up is the value of $\pink{\text{Duration}}$ when $\blue{\text{Pages}}$ is $\blue 0$. We can extend the table according to its rate to find this value:  


[[☃ image 1]]

This means that the second printer takes $\pink{20}$ seconds to warm up.

**Since $\green{30}>\green{20}$, the first printer takes more time to warm up.**

The second column is labeled Duration, which contains the values 20, 40, 60, and 80. Between each number is an arrow pointing to the previous number labeled minus 20.

hints.content:
In $100$ seconds, the first printer warms up for $30$ seconds and then prints for $100-30=70$ seconds. We are given that it prints $\green{1}$ page per second, so it prints a total of $\blue{70}$ pages in $\pink{100}$ seconds.

We can extend the table of the second printer according to its rate of change to find the value of $\blue{\text{Pages}}$ when $\pink{\text{Duration}}$ is $\pink{100}$:

Pages | Duration
-:|-: 
$0$ | $20$
$+16\downarrow$ | $+20\downarrow$
$16$ | $40$
$+16\downarrow$ | $+20\downarrow$
$32$ | $60$
$+16\downarrow$ | $+20\downarrow$
$48$ | $80$
$+16\downarrow$ | $+20\downarrow$
$64$ | $100$

This means that the second printer prints a total of $\blue{64}$ pages in $\pink{100}$ seconds.

**Since $\blue{70}>\blue{64}$, the first printer prints more pages in $100$ seconds.**

Let's sum it up:

- The first printer takes more time to warm up.

- The first printer prints more pages in $100$ seconds.

question.content:
Heloïse considered two types of printers for her office. Each printer needs some time to warm up before it starts printing at a constant rate.

The first printer takes $30$ seconds to warm up, and then it prints $1$ page per second.

The printing duration (in seconds) of the second printer as a function of the number of pages is given by the following table of values:

$\text{Pages}$  | $\text{Duration}$ (seconds)
:-: | :-:
$16$ | $40$
$32$ | $60$
$48$ | $80$

**Which printer takes more time to warm up?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

**Which printer prints more pages in $100$ seconds?**

[[☃ radio 2]]

choices.content: They both take the same time to warm up
They both print the same number of pages in $100$ seconds
